resources.string: Sound travels down the ear canal
The outer ear gathers sound. Pressure waves travel through the ear canal to the eardrum.
The eardrum vibrates. The malleus, incus, and stapes transfer this motion to the oval window at the entrance to the cochlea.
A wave travels through the cochlea
Movement at the oval window sets cochlear fluid in motion, causing a wave along the basilar membrane. The membrane responds most to higher pitches near the base and to lower pitches toward the apex.
Hair cells turn motion into a signal
The hair bundle tilts and opens mechanically sensitive channels. Inner hair cells release a chemical messenger at their synapses, activating nearby auditory nerve fibers.
The auditory nerve carries electrical impulses to the brainstem. After several relays, signals reach the auditory cortex, where the brain helps interpret sound.
Motion is slowed and enlarged. The pathway is schematic. No sound is played, and this is not a hearing test.
